item.title: Is China easing some online censorship?
item.description:
China

China | Media control Sep 24th 2026 “Treating differing voices as floods and terrifying beasts is a fundamental misunderstanding of the nature of governance,” would be an unsurprising homily from a liberal newspaper in a democracy. From the actual source, Qiushi, the Chinese Communist Party’s ma...
item.content:encoded:
Is China easing some online censorship?

China | Media control

Sep 24th 2026

“Treating differing voices as floods and terrifying beasts is a fundamental misunderstanding of the nature of governance,” would be an unsurprising homily from a liberal newspaper in a democracy. From the actual source, Qiushi, the Chinese Communist Party’s main theoretical journal, in September, it is positively startling. Other party outlets have been sounding similarly enlightened. “Wherever energy is spent on targeting the commenter and blocking channels of speech, almost without exception the result is an even greater crisis of trust,” said China Youth Daily, run by the Communist Youth League, in July. Some officials “seek only silence in public discourse, not the resolution of problems, and habitually block and delete posts instead of solving issues”, China Comment, a magazine run by the country’s official news agency, Xinhua, also weighed in that month.

Is China going through one of the post-Mao era’s occasional phases when liberals in the establishment push back against conservatives through articles like these? Far from it. Since Xi Jinping took power in 2012, liberals have been all but silenced. And censors have been as frantic as ever of late in their efforts to scrub the internet clean of grumbling about officialdom. In July news turned viral online of a parking-space dispute between an ordinary citizen and a cadre. The censors deleted suggestions that an inquiry may have been rigged in the official’s favour. The police are ever vigilant, too. Dare to post a message online that the death toll in last month’s flash flood on the Nepal-China border was higher in China than reported? Seven days in jail for that. A system that brooks no dissent is behaving true to form.

But China’s leaders do sometimes worry that censorship can go too far. Overly tight restrictions on everyday moaning, they suggest, can make it harder to get the feedback they need to improve government behaviour and thereby defuse public grievances before they explode on the streets. In China, calibrating how much censorship to apply is an art that officials often struggle to master in a way that pleases their bosses. In recent months several articles in state media have implied that many are not doing it right.

Officials would be correct to think that Mr Xi prefers them to err on the side of caution when deciding whether to censor. “Unhealthy discourse can become a narcotic for the public, a social divider, a soft knife that kills and a catalyst for unrest,” he told media bosses a decade ago.

But Mr Xi may now want some fine-tuning. Examples of over-censorship given by the media imply that his concerns relate to the deletion of comments that reflect badly on local officials. There is no hint that he wants to encourage criticism of the party, let alone of himself. China Comment cited several examples of excessive twitchiness by officials, such as their blocking in May of a person’s social-media account for posting a complaint on a local tourism department’s account about the cleanliness of seating at a concert. Another involved someone who last year posted a video online of a woman trying to assert her right of way on a narrow road by flashing her husband’s law-enforcement credentials. Police put pressure on the citizen to delete the footage. He did so, but later reposted an edited version that drew 10m views.

Mr Xi will hardly be surprised by such stories. Local governments often go to great lengths to prevent higher levels from learning about their mistakes. During Mr Xi’s rule, many authorities have used the achievement of “zero public-opinion [incidents]” to assess whether officials are fit for promotion. “The obsession with zero public opinion has given rise to a bizarre and inverted approach to handling public complaints, resulting in multiple deep-seated governance problems with significant harm,” thundered an article on the website of the party’s main mouthpiece, the People’s Daily, in July. Local officials, however, will remain cautious. ■

Subscribers can sign up to Drum Tower, our new weekly newsletter, to understand what the world makes of China—and what China makes of the world.

item.title: What Mao can teach China about managing America
item.description:
China

China | Chaguan Sep 24th 2026 TRADE WAR. Tech war. New cold war. All of these shorthand descriptions for frayed Sino-American ties have an air of foreboding. Not so the label that the two countries agreed on earlier this year, at China’s urging. They are now officially in a “constructive relatio...
item.content:encoded:
What Mao can teach China about managing America

China | Chaguan

Sep 24th 2026

TRADE WAR. Tech war. New cold war. All of these shorthand descriptions for frayed Sino-American ties have an air of foreboding. Not so the label that the two countries agreed on earlier this year, at China’s urging. They are now officially in a “constructive relationship of strategic stability”. If that fails to set your pulse racing, the cumbersome phrase has succeeded: it is meant to signify a calm approach for managing the superpowers’ tensions.

More candid, and more alarming, is how many thinkers in China now describe its relationship with America. Instead of strategic stability, they call it a “strategic stalemate”—a loaded term in China, evoking not diplomacy but a struggle for the upper hand. Among those to do so recently: advisers to the Chinese cabinet, researchers under the Ministry of State Security, and scholars at leading universities. Familiar to many in China, the words are drawn from Mao Zedong’s “On Protracted War” speeches, delivered in the remote Communist base of Yan’an in 1938.

Mao’s musings nine decades ago should not be given undue weight. But the protracted-war framework yields valuable insights about how China views its contest with America and offers clues to how things might develop. With Xi Jinping about to hold talks with Donald Trump in Washington as The Economist went to press, the old dictator’s words in his guerrilla days are of interest.

Mao argued that in the first phase of a long war against a technologically superior adversary, scrappy revolutionaries must hunker down in defence. The next phase is strategic stalemate: the overstretched adversary can no longer advance and the revolutionary forces get better organised. Then comes the final phase, the counter-offensive, when the once-weaker revolutionaries rout the once-stronger enemy.

So declaring that China and America have reached strategic stalemate is freighted with significance. No one doubts which of the two powers is to be seen as the weary incumbent and which the energetic revolutionary. The trade war started in 2018, when Mr Trump slapped an initial batch of tariffs on China. For the rest of his first term, China was on the back foot. It was not entirely quiet, hitting back at America with its own tariffs. But it settled for a lopsided deal that if implemented in full would have led to China buying far more American goods and opening more widely to American investors. In Maoist terms, the deal showed “the courage to retreat”, often necessary in the first phase of protracted war.

The point of retreat is not to give up but to conserve resources for a fightback. This is precisely what China did throughout Joe Biden’s presidency. Keenly aware of where America had immense leverage—notably, in advanced semiconductors—Chinese officials redoubled efforts to cultivate domestic alternatives, no matter how expensive. They also honed their counter-attack, creating a stronger system of export controls and tightening their grip on the Chinese companies that mine and process critical minerals. When Mr Trump returned to office and cranked up tariffs, his officials were astonished by the ferocity of China’s pushback. In blocking the exports of minerals, especially rare earths, China threatened to bring swathes of American industry to a halt.

It has become commonplace to say that the superpowers have achieved rough parity in their ability to harm each other. America has computer chips; China has rare earths. Analysts call it “mutually assured disruption” or a “balance of vulnerability”, as if the two countries are, in economic terms, basically equal. The “strategic stalemate” framing gets at something more profound about this parity: to have come this far is already progress for China.

One obvious question is whether Mr Xi has designs on the third stage of the “protracted war”—a full-blown counter-offensive. Last year when trade hostilities with America were at their most intense, state media urged the public to revisit Mao’s speeches, to boost confidence in China’s resilience. Yet the parallels with the great helmsman’s analysis go only so far. Most Chinese thinkers believe it is impossible to score a decisive, enduring economic victory over America. Maintaining a strategic stalemate looks like a more realistic objective. Huang Renwei of Shanghai’s Fudan University has said, hopefully, that it can last for 30 years.

The trouble with a stalemate is that it may prove short-lived. Both countries want to break out of it and are seeking new ways to gain an advantage—and are alert to risks that might pin them down. Fear of being permanently reduced to an inferior position in artificial intelligence is one reason why China is reluctant to embrace AI safety regimes proposed by America. Until Chinese AI models are as powerful as America’s—ie, until they have reached a stalemate in AI—China appears unwilling to slow its AI labs down.

The fragility of the stalemate also explains why China has continued to restrain rare-earth exports to America and its allies, especially Japan. If the two superpowers truly enjoyed a constructive relationship, as they claim, China could have created a transparent, efficient licensing system for global companies seeking rare earths. Instead their relationship is marred by mistrust, and China knows that throttling the supply of rare earths is the swiftest way it can discipline Mr Trump if he turns more aggressive again.

More dismally for China, another aspect of Mao’s stalemate phase also applies today. He warned it would be “a very painful period for China”, during which “pessimism will grow”. The echoes with the economic situation today are clear. A relentless focus on technological self-reliance has helped insulate China from American pressure. But Chinese people have paid the price, their income growth slowing as the state channels money into industrial capacity rather than social welfare. It resembles the economy of a country at war—and a protracted war at that. ■

item.title: A contentious battle in Alaska may determine control of the Senate
item.description:
United States

United States | Rough waters Sep 24th 2026 Alaska is an unusual state with unusual politics. It is both tiny and enormous, with fewer than 740,000 people living in a territory more than twice the size of Texas. It is staunchly Republican yet politically open. The last Democratic presidential can...
item.content:encoded:
A contentious battle in Alaska may determine control of the Senate

United States | Rough waters

Sep 24th 2026

Alaska is an unusual state with unusual politics. It is both tiny and enormous, with fewer than 740,000 people living in a territory more than twice the size of Texas. It is staunchly Republican yet politically open. The last Democratic presidential candidate to win Alaskans’ vote was Lyndon Johnson, in 1964, but the state prizes moderation. Now America’s 49th state is one of a handful that will determine if Democrats win the Senate.

The Senate campaign, between Dan Sullivan, a Republican incumbent, and Mary Peltola, a former Democratic congresswoman, is a toss-up, and may become more contentious still. On September 23rd the New York Times published an investigation about Ms Peltola, alleging chaotic mismanagement and mistreatment of her staff. Her campaign denies any pattern of abuse. The allegations are particularly jarring for a candidate whose appeal to voters was built, in large part, on her charisma and approachability.

Democrats hope that Alaska’s unique political culture and the outsized impact of Donald Trump’s policies on the state will help to bolster Ms Peltola’s chances. But much depends on Ms Peltola, too.

The Economist’s forecast model, which does not yet account for the Times report, puts her odds of victory at 56%. That she has even a chance is a reminder of how, in a partisan era, Alaska’s politics have remained remarkably fluid. In 2010 Lisa Murkowski, Alaska’s other Republican senator and a centrist, lost to a Tea Party candidate in the primary, then won the first write-in Senate campaign in more than 50 years. The ruling majority in the statehouse is a “tripartisan” coalition of Democrats, Republicans and non-partisans. Alaska is the only state that combines a non-partisan primary with ranked-choice voting. “When it comes down to it, parties really don’t play an important role,” says Gary Stevens, the state Senate president who worked alongside Ms Peltola in the legislature in the early aughts.

Ms Peltola is a product of this environment. A native Alaskan who captained her first fishing boat at 14, she won statewide office in 2022, when she beat Sarah Palin, a former governor, to represent Alaska in Congress. Ms Peltola and Ms Murkowski endorsed each other that year. Mr Sullivan’s campaign ads try to portray Ms Peltola as a puppet for “Lower 48 liberals”, but she often bucks her party—the National Rifle Association supported her in 2024.

She is also happy, on occasion, to side with the president. Mr Sullivan argues that Ms Peltola and a Democratic Senate majority would restrict leasing and drilling in the Arctic. “My opponent would ally herself with the anti-Alaska energy groups in Congress, who will do what they always do: shut down Alaska energy,” he said in a debate on Kodiak Island on September 12th. Ms Peltola has released a pro-oil ad in which she promises that she will “work with Donald Trump to unlock more land and more development”.

On other issues, Ms Peltola criticises the effect of Mr Trump’s policies on Alaska, if not Mr Trump himself. The president carried the state by 13 points in 2024, so Ms Peltola must win over many Trump voters if she is to eke out a victory.

Despite the state’s oil riches, Alaskans are particularly affected by pricey fuel, which raises the cost of heating rural villages, transporting goods and people over long distances and, of course, fishing. Because Kodiak Island is a fishing hub, the entire debate was devoted to fisheries issues. Fuel “is the number one cost for all fishermen”, Ms Peltola told the crowd. “We are being priced out of petroleum, and we’re being priced out of our lives in Alaska because of the war in Iran.” In the state’s survey of Alaska’s rural communities this summer, average petrol costs were $7.56, almost twice the national average.

Alaskans have also been particularly affected by the Department of Government Efficiency’s dismantling of the federal bureaucracy. The Alaska Department of Labour and Workforce Development reckons the state lost nearly 5% of its federal workforce in 2025, a higher share than any state other than Maryland and New Mexico. Federal employment in Alaska is now at its lowest level in over 35 years.

Take fishing, again. Officials and fishermen rely on data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to set seasonal fishing quotas, track fish stocks and monitor the weather. NOAA’s lab on the Kodiak Archipelago, which surveys crab in the Bering Sea, lost a third of its scientists last year to firings, buyouts or early retirements, according to Mike Litzow, its former director. The administration’s hostility towards the federal bureaucracy also, ironically, increased the lab’s administrative burdens. To get on the boat to survey crab “requires something like 12 layers of approval”, Mr Litzow adds. Every purchase made with a government credit card was subject to scrutiny. “Someone who worked for me had a credit-card packet with 15 purchases for the month, and the packet was 385 pages of documentation,” he recalls.

Frustration with high fuel prices or unreliable weather data, the Peltola campaign hopes, will overshadow any reports of mismanagement or outbursts, though the race is close enough that negative news may have an impact. In such a big state, with many remote communities, Kodiak’s fishermen were pleased to see their candidates show up to seek their votes. Several fishermen at the debate who identified as Republican said they view Ms Peltola as one of them. The rubber boots she wore on stage probably didn’t hurt.■

Stay on top of American politics with The US in brief, our daily newsletter with fast analysis of the most important political news, and Checks and Balance, a weekly note that examines the state of American democracy and the issues that matter to voters.

item.title: 为穷人办的学校不是差学校
item.description:
United States

美国 | 问题不在于钱 2026年9月24日 在2020年达到顶峰的“觉醒”意识形态——一种以种族和性别为核心的思想——并没有领袖，但妮可·汉娜-琼斯可以说是其最具代表性的知识分子。作为《纽约时报杂志》的记者，她撰写了《1619项目》，一部以奴隶制为中心的美国修正主义历史，并因其2016年一篇关于将女儿送入一所主要招收贫困非白人学生的学校的报道而赢得赞誉。她于9月20日发表的最新文章是一次部分自我批评，引发了大量反“觉醒”的幸灾乐祸。文章讲述了她女儿随后遭遇的教师缺勤或不负责任、同学吵闹的困境，以及她对自己为了以一人之力修复破碎系统这一渺茫希望而牺牲女儿教育感到愤怒。然而，即使汉娜-琼斯女士...
item.content:encoded:
为穷人办的学校不是差学校

美国 | 问题不在于钱 2026年9月24日 在2020年达到顶峰的“觉醒”意识形态——一种以种族和性别为核心的思想——并没有领袖，但妮可·汉娜-琼斯可以说是其最具代表性的知识分子。作为《纽约时报杂志》的记者，她撰写了《1619项目》，一部以奴隶制为中心的美国修正主义历史，并因其2016年一篇关于将女儿送入一所主要招收贫困非白人学生的学校的报道而赢得赞誉。她于9月20日发表的最新文章是一次部分自我批评，引发了大量反“觉醒”的幸灾乐祸。文章讲述了她女儿随后遭遇的教师缺勤或不负责任、同学吵闹的困境，以及她对自己为了以一人之力修复破碎系统这一渺茫希望而牺牲女儿教育感到愤怒。然而，即使汉娜-琼斯女士为这种对孩子的“背叛”承担了个人责任，她却很少提及那些可能对她女儿就读学校的功能失调起了作用的、由进步派支持的教育政策。此外，她对学校失败提供的主要解释已经过时了几十年。 汉娜-琼斯女士引用了倡导组织EdBuild在2019年的一项研究，该研究报告称“在全国范围内，以非白人为主的学区的年资金比以白人为主的学区少230亿美元”。由此她得出结论，此类学校糟糕的考试成绩仅仅“反映”了这种财政“劣势”。她几乎找不到比女儿就读的纽约公立学校第307分校更糟糕的例子来支持这一说法了——该校在2024-25学年每名学生花费52349美元，使其成为美国开支最高的学区之一中资金最充足的学校之一。而PS 307并非例外，反而是全国模式的极端例子：白人学生比例最低的公立学校实际上获得的资金最多。 认为贫困地区学校资金不足的观点有其历史依据。1940年，68%的学校预算来自地方来源，如房产税。但自20世纪60年代开始的一系列再分配改革，用州政府资金补充了这些经费，并在较小程度上用联邦资金补充——这些资金主要拨给贫困学区（且未计入EdBuild的研究）。根据智库布鲁金斯学会最近的一项研究，早在1976-77学年，最贫困、白人学生最少的那五分之一学区的人均支出就最高。这一模式在2020-21学年依然成立——即使考虑到以非白人为主的学区（往往位于大城市）普遍工资水平更高之后也是如此，并且随后由于民主党在新冠时期的财政刺激计划而得到加强。《经济学人》的分析发现，2024年，在调整工资差异后，黑人学生所在学区的平均人均支出比白人学生所在学区高出3.5%。西语裔学生的相应优势为0.9%。 然而，这些支出并未带来平等的学习成果。在2024年针对13至14岁学生的全国阅读和数学测试中，白人学生平均得分处于第58百分位，而黑人考生平均处于第32百分位。这一差距部分源于黑人学生更可能贫困，因此更可能有更大的教育需求，这可能为更积极的资金分配提供理由。像PS 307这样的学校往往有更多有学习障碍的儿童，他们需要更多专家来帮助家庭环境困难的学生和正在学习英语的学生。 然而，教育学者也强调了资金之外的一系列问题，其中大多数在汉娜-琼斯女士的叙述中显而易见。加入工会的教师的薪酬主要基于资历，而非业绩或学校环境的艰苦程度。因此，贫困地区的教师往往会流向纪律问题较少、更富裕地区的学校，给他们原来所在的学校留下一扇旋转门，使那里充斥着缺乏经验的教师。经常缺勤或学生表现不佳的教师之所以能留在课堂上，是因为他们难以被替换。尽管学生在标准化考试中分数很低仍被升入更高年级——汉娜-琼斯女士曾说这些考试衡量的是特权而非智力或学校质量——这使得学生没有意识到自己并未掌握所学内容。而对扰乱秩序的学生不予纪律处分或将他们移出课堂，则妨碍了所有同学的学习努力。 汉娜-琼斯女士的许多批评者仍然称赞她公开反省。但她的寓言故事给我们的主要教训，并不是每个有办法逃离此类学校的家长都应该这样做，而是要听从她女儿第二所学校校长的信息：对非白人学生“降低期望”是“披着反种族主义外衣的种族主义”。■ 通过我们的每日通讯《美国简报》——快速分析最重要的政治新闻——以及每周通讯《制衡》——审视美国民主状况和对选民重要的问题——保持对美国政治的掌握。

item.title: Donald Trump will lose his latest media battle
item.description:
United States

United States | On mute Sep 24th 2026 He was uncharacteristically silent as he cut the ribbon on a new helipad at the White House on September 21st. Donald Trump’s mouth moved, but viewers heard nothing. The press “pool” that normally relays the president’s public remarks was absent. Mr Trump ha...
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump will lose his latest media battle

United States | On mute

Sep 24th 2026

He was uncharacteristically silent as he cut the ribbon on a new helipad at the White House on September 21st. Donald Trump’s mouth moved, but viewers heard nothing. The press “pool” that normally relays the president’s public remarks was absent. Mr Trump had been muted by his latest skirmish with the press.

The dispute began days earlier, when Mr Trump announced that he would ban CNN and MS NOW, two cable-news networks, and Politico, a news outlet, from the White House. There was “no reason”, he said later. “It’s really just cumulative stories over the last two years. You get sick of it.” In response, America’s five big television networks—ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN and Fox News—said they would boycott some coverage of Mr Trump. Those five comprise the White House’s television pool, taking turns filming the president and sharing the footage with other news organisations.

The relationship between the press and the presidency is inherently fractious. Even so, excluding outlets because of their coverage constitutes “viewpoint discrimination”, which is barred by the First Amendment. On September 24th a federal judge said the administration had not followed due process and ordered it to temporarily lift the ban on the outlets.

In this battle, as in others, Mr Trump craves victory, but merely starting the fight has an impact. Last year, after the Pentagon imposed new restrictions on journalists, much of its traditional press corps left and was replaced by influencers and once-fringe outlets. In March a federal judge deemed the restrictions unconstitutional. Courts are also weighing a dispute between Mr Trump and the Associated Press, which was barred from some events and Air Force One after refusing to call the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America”.

The president himself has sued almost a dozen journalists and outlets since he first took office. Most cases have been dismissed, but two were settled on terms favourable to him. ABC agreed to pay $15m towards Mr Trump’s presidential library, plus $1m in legal fees, and expressed “regret” over remarks by George Stephanopoulos, a presenter. Paramount Skydance, CBS’s owner, agreed to pay $16m towards the library to settle another case. Brendan Carr, chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, has threatened broadcasters with scrutiny of their licences over programming Mr Trump dislikes.

Fears about the politicisation of news helped prompt a dozen Democratic state attorneys-general to oppose Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, which owns CNN. Paramount is run by David Ellison, who reportedly assured administration officials that he would make “sweeping changes” to CNN. He had already installed Bari Weiss, a critic of the left, as editor-in-chief of CBS News. On September 21st the attorneys-general allowed the deal to proceed, with one of the conditions being that Paramount appoint an “editorial independence” board for CNN and CBS.

The point of Mr Trump’s campaign is not necessarily to win each fight but to wear the enemy down. Americans’ trust in the news is fading, with many relying on social media for information. Mr Trump’s ally Elon Musk owns X, one of the biggest platforms, and the president offers rambling monologues on his own Truth Social site. A new poll from the Pew Research Centre finds that Americans broadly support a free press, but most say the government should be able to restrict it in certain circumstances, such as if it contains inaccuracies. To Mr Trump, that may sound like an invitation to wield a bigger gag. ■

item.title: Why licence-plate readers are angering Americans
item.description:
United States

United States | What the Flock? Sep 24th 2026 AMERICANS DO NOT like to be watched. Neither, it seems, do the bosses of companies that make surveillance technology. Josh Hawley, a Republican senator from Missouri, invited several of them to testify to a subcommittee about their products on Septem...
item.content:encoded:
Why licence-plate readers are angering Americans

United States | What the Flock?

Sep 24th 2026

AMERICANS DO NOT like to be watched. Neither, it seems, do the bosses of companies that make surveillance technology. Josh Hawley, a Republican senator from Missouri, invited several of them to testify to a subcommittee about their products on September 23rd, amid mounting privacy concerns. All declined.

His request follows months of backlash against Flock Safety, America’s largest operator of automatic licence-plate readers (ALPRs). Flock’s cameras use AI to track vehicles, aiding police investigations. But officers have also misused them. The share of Americans opposed to ALPRs in their community has risen from 33% to 46% in under a year, according to YouGov, a pollster. Lawmakers from both parties are mulling bills to limit the technology.

ALPRs are not new: local governments have long used them to collect tolls and enforce traffic laws. More recently, activists on the left protested against their use by federal immigration authorities. Donald Trump, on the other hand, says he likes Flock because it helps law enforcement. Yet the uproar has escalated quickly, echoing the outcry over data centres. ALPRs and data centres have both scaled up quickly and become symbols of anxiety about AI.

Flock, which sells cameras much cheaper than its competitors’, boasts more than 120,000 across the country, each generating millions of images. Owners can share this data with nearby police departments and Flock’s nationwide database, allowing officers to search different cities or states. AI can extract other details about a vehicle, such as its colour, broadening searches beyond licence plates.

Police say this helps them solve crimes such as theft or abductions. Flock claims to have aided 10,000 missing-person cases last year. But its network of ALPRs “goes far beyond what people previously understood the tools to be”, argues Melissa Owen of the National Association of Criminal Defence Lawyers. Cops do not need warrants to look up plates, and state laws vary on how officers log searches, how long data can be stored and whether footage can be sent to other states.

Officers have been caught stalking ex-partners and tracking spouses. Software errors have led to innocent drivers being stopped. A lack of transparency has added to the furore. The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), a digital-rights group, analysed search logs and found officers entering nonsensical reasons for looking up plates, including “LOL” and “sexy”. (Flock has since added a drop-down menu of categories.) The EFF is one of several organisations suing cities for allegedly running thousands of unnecessary searches. The company says it has tightened requirements for searching its database.

However, the uproar has spilled into the midterms. Seth Bodnar, an independent running for the Senate in Montana, recently filmed himself shooting a camera with a shotgun. The backlash is producing more substantive results, too. Greg Abbott, running to be re-elected as Texas’s governor, has paused state funding for Flock. Over 250 cities, towns and schools ended their contracts with Flock in August and September, according to a tracker by Secure Justice, an anti-surveillance group. In the same two months last year it was five. ■

item.title: 白宫可能很快宣布一项荒谬的柴油出口禁令
item.description:
United States

美国 | 愚蠢的想法 2026年9月24日 当选民对一个问题的愤怒高涨时——尤其是在选举之前——政客们通常会试图解决它。理想情况下，他们提出的补救措施应当是明智的。但有时，看似在政治上有效的解决方案，在实质上却荒谬至极。柴油的情况正是如此。9月20日，美国柴油平均价格创下每加仑6.50美元的历史新高。这对于依赖柴油的美国人是痛苦的。而对于共和党议员来说，这是一场政治噩梦，他们本已因伊朗战争和高昂的汽油价格而面临公众愤怒。越来越多的共和党人正在推动禁止柴油出口，包括竞选密歇根州参议院席位的共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，以及在阿拉斯加州面临艰难连任竞选的共和党参议员丹·沙利文。9月22日，唐纳德·特朗普...
item.content:encoded:
白宫可能很快宣布一项荒谬的柴油出口禁令

美国 | 愚蠢的想法 2026年9月24日

当选民对一个问题的愤怒高涨时——尤其是在选举之前——政客们通常会试图解决它。理想情况下，他们提出的补救措施应当是明智的。但有时，看似在政治上有效的解决方案，在实质上却荒谬至极。柴油的情况正是如此。9月20日，美国柴油平均价格创下每加仑6.50美元的历史新高。这对于依赖柴油的美国人是痛苦的。而对于共和党议员来说，这是一场政治噩梦，他们本已因伊朗战争和高昂的汽油价格而面临公众愤怒。越来越多的共和党人正在推动禁止柴油出口，包括竞选密歇根州参议院席位的共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，以及在阿拉斯加州面临艰难连任竞选的共和党参议员丹·沙利文。9月22日，唐纳德·特朗普表示他正在考虑这一想法。次日，新闻媒体Politico报道称，政府正准备实施一项为期90天的限制措施，尽管白宫随后否认了该报道。如果这样的限制措施真的实施，它对解决问题几乎毫无帮助——反而可能制造新的问题。

要理解为何出口禁令是不明智的，不妨听听特朗普自己的能源部长克里斯·赖特在9月23日由《经济学人》组织的活动上所说的话。“禁止柴油出口这种生硬工具绝对行不通，”他解释道。“生产柴油的同一家炼油厂也生产汽油和喷气燃料，所以如果你不能出口炼油厂生产的柴油，储存空间就会耗尽，你就必须减少美国的炼油量，这会给汽油价格和喷气燃料价格带来上行压力。”这给共和党人带来了一些挑战。首先，关于炼油厂运作方式的详细解释并不能成为引人注目的竞选广告素材。但柴油价格高昂的问题可能会变得更加严重。柴油的需求尤其缺乏弹性。与通常用于休闲驾车出行的汽油不同，柴油主要被用于关键的经济活动，为拖拉机、卡车、挖掘机等提供动力。而且，恰好在拥有重要参议院选举的州，包括阿拉斯加和爱荷华，柴油使用量特别高。柴油供应可能继续受到制约，因为正如一位交易员所言，“如今最稀缺的大宗商品不是原油，而是炼油产能。”与伊朗的战争严重扰乱了海湾地区的炼油和柴油运输。乌克兰战争也对柴油造成了不成比例的影响——柴油长期以来是俄罗斯的重要出口产品——因为乌克兰加大了对俄罗斯炼油厂的轰炸力度。综合来看，来自俄罗斯和海湾地区的柴油运输量自去年以来下降了75%，且不太可能迅速反弹。

因此，难怪政客们正在考虑禁令，尽管政府内部在争论要走到哪一步，石油行业则在激烈游说反对。赖特先生建议，政府或许可以寻求通过与公司以“更简单、自愿、合作的方式”合作来减少柴油出口，而不是彻底禁止。真正的禁令会引发赖特先生所指出的问题，给汽油价格带来上行压力。它还会造成其他麻烦，让人们对美国作为能源出口供应国和投资目的地的可靠性产生新的怀疑。但这些其他问题是长期性的，而中期选举不到六周就要举行了。■

通过我们的每日通讯《美国简报》（快速分析最重要的政治新闻）和每周专栏《制衡》（审视美国民主状况以及对选民重要的问题），随时了解美国政治动态。

item.title: Donald Trump’s least favourite thing
item.description:
United States

United States | Hot air Sep 24th 2026 CLIMATE WEEK NYC is held alongside the UN General Assembly each September, when leaders gather in New York to discuss some of the world’s most intractable challenges. For Donald Trump, climate change isn’t on the list. He mentioned it in his speech to the Un...
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump’s least favourite thing

United States | Hot air

Sep 24th 2026

CLIMATE WEEK NYC is held alongside the UN General Assembly each September, when leaders gather in New York to discuss some of the world’s most intractable challenges. For Donald Trump, climate change isn’t on the list. He mentioned it in his speech to the United Nations on September 22nd only to characterise it as a hoax; in last year’s address, he called it the “greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world”. Policymakers have long discussed how governments can unleash renewable energy; Mr Trump is now providing a study of how to restrain it.

“My goal”, he said at the start of this year, “is to not let any windmill be built.” Some tactics have been expected, such as the Republican tax law that ended Biden-era tax credits for wind and solar farms. Other methods have been more creative, such as paying wind developers to abandon offshore projects, a practice over which the attorneys-general of California and New York filed suit on September 22nd. Mr Trump has not succeeded in halting all renewable development, but he is slowing it down.

The president’s main problems with wind and solar were summarised in an executive order last year titled “Ending Market Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign-Controlled Energy Sources”. It is correct that wind and solar produce intermittent power, depend on foreign supply-chains and benefit from public support. Yet by the government’s own figures the “levelised” cost of electricity—ie, over an asset’s lifespan—from onshore wind and solar is now lower than that of natural gas, and there would be ways to manage intermittency (through energy storage and complementary sources) and foreign dependence (through trade deals with allies). Mr Trump is unconvinced. Chris Wright, his energy secretary, emphasises the need for consistent power, of the kind generated by natural gas and coal. “If you produce electricity only some of the time, and we don’t know when,” Mr Wright argued on September 23rd, “that’s not firm electric generation.”

Installations of utility-scale solar have dipped, in part due to permitting bottlenecks and shifting rules on imported equipment—last year’s tax law included provisions to determine if a project was supported by a “prohibited foreign entity”. But the president harbours a specific disdain for wind turbines. He blames them for killing birds, slashing property values, causing cancer and generally being “inappropriate” and “pathetic”. Offshore wind has proven particularly vulnerable, due to its high cost of $119 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $77 for natural gas, as well as lengthy timelines and dependence on federal permitting.

On Mr Trump’s first day of his second term, he issued a memorandum temporarily halting permits for wind deployment on federal land and waters, which included all sites appropriate for offshore wind. Then, in December, the Department of the Interior suspended the leases for five offshore wind projects that had received permits during the presidency of Joe Biden.

Judges have allowed construction to resume, but beyond those five, says Harrison Sholler of BloombergNEF, a data outfit, no more are expected to come online by 2035. So far this year the government has paid about $3.9bn to firms to abandon their planned projects offshore, using taxpayer money supposed to settle lawsuits against the government. Inflation and high interest rates had already made those projects less attractive; uncertainty around state support made matters worse. Patrick Pouyanné of TotalEnergies, the first to strike a deal, explained the effects of shifting policy on long-term offshore projects: “it doesn’t work.”

Onshore wind is cheaper, at $57/MWh, and has fared better. There was a surge in building this year, as developers scurried to claim tax credits before they expired. But BloombergNEF has lowered its forecast for 2029 by 25% compared with its outlook from April 2025. On top of expiring tax credits and the pause on federal permitting, developers are now grappling with delays from the Department of War (DoW). Wind projects have long required approval from the Department of Defence, now the DoW, to ensure that they do not interfere with radar or flight paths. But from August 2025, the DoW gradually stopped reviewing proposals. Since then, says Jason Grumet of the American Clean Power Association, a trade group, “they’ve just turned off the lights and pulled the blinds. They’re cancelling meetings.” Over 150 projects are caught in the bottleneck, which the DoW argues is justified on national-security grounds.

As Mr Trump continues to clamp down on renewables, two forces may lift them up. One judge has ordered the administration to resume reviews of projects delayed by the DoW, and another has indicated that the restriction of permits on federal lands may be illegal. More important, there is booming demand for power. “There’s a certain point”, argues Mr Grumet, “at which the price increases and what we fear will be energy-adequacy challenges will force any administration to get behind an all-of-the-above policy.”■

item.title: 缅因州风向，参议院风向
item.description:
United States

美国 | 列克星敦 2026年9月24日 如果你来自一个你的政党拥有决定性优势的州，并且你喜欢高谈阔论，那么担任美国参议员可能是一份轻松的美差。按照党团领袖的指示投票；不要给你的初选挑战者留下任何空间——如果你是共和党人，就向右靠；如果你是民主党人，就向左靠；定期出现在福克斯新闻或MS Now上，痛斥对方政党。然后就可以高枕无忧，看着金主的钱滚滚而来，展望你在那个曾经被称为世界上最伟大的审议机构——如今已变成最豪华养老院——的黄金岁月。 当然，有些参议员倾向于比这努力得多。而至少有一位参议员——共和党人苏珊·柯林斯——别无选择。自1997年以来，她代表缅因州，而该州自1988年以来从未在总统...
item.content:encoded:
缅因州风向，参议院风向

美国 | 列克星敦 2026年9月24日

如果你来自一个你的政党拥有决定性优势的州，并且你喜欢高谈阔论，那么担任美国参议员可能是一份轻松的美差。按照党团领袖的指示投票；不要给你的初选挑战者留下任何空间——如果你是共和党人，就向右靠；如果你是民主党人，就向左靠；定期出现在福克斯新闻或MS Now上，痛斥对方政党。然后就可以高枕无忧，看着金主的钱滚滚而来，展望你在那个曾经被称为世界上最伟大的审议机构——如今已变成最豪华养老院——的黄金岁月。

当然，有些参议员倾向于比这努力得多。而至少有一位参议员——共和党人苏珊·柯林斯——别无选择。自1997年以来，她代表缅因州，而该州自1988年以来从未在总统选举中投票给共和党。她是最后一批与来自不同党派的参议员共享一个州的罕见人物之一，在她的情况下，那位是同民主党党团合作的独立人士安格斯·金。所谓的“分裂代表团”曾经很常见。从1969年到1994年，至少有20个州，最多时达27个州，拥有分裂代表团；就在2013年，还有18对这样的“古怪搭档”，他们通常学会为了本州的利益而合作，有时甚至为了国家的利益。现在只剩下4个，这是自1913年参议员直接选举开始以来的最少数量——这还包括佛蒙特州，那里的分裂是在民主党人彼得·韦尔奇和伯尼·桑德斯之间，后者作为独立人士，是民主党人，但更“纯粹”的民主党人。

这是一个比众议院选区划分不公更难解决的两极分化的结果和原因。不再是政客通过把选民分入选区来挑选选民，而是美国人按党派将自己分入各州，同时随着所有政治都变得全国化，减少分票投票。柯林斯通过勤勉的选民服务逆势而行，为州里带来联邦项目，并创下了参议员连续投票超过10,000次无缺席的历史纪录。像她这样的参议员最难的一点，是在所有这些投票中走出自己的道路，展现出足够的独立性以吸引中间派甚至一些民主党人，同时又不疏远她的共和党基本盘。

《班戈每日新闻》8月份的一项分析发现，柯林斯在其职业生涯中很少投出反对本党的决定性票，但她的次数比任何其他党派的参议员都多，包括2021年国会山遇袭后投票支持给唐纳德·特朗普定罪。13年来，她一直在卢加中心这个非营利组织和乔治城大学公共政策学院共同维护的年度“两党指数”中位列共和党参议员之首。现在，似乎每六年一次，柯林斯都处于她职业生涯中最艰难的竞选之中。尽管她支持堕胎权，但她投票确认了布雷特·卡瓦诺担任最高法院大法官，称她相信他会将罗诉韦德案视为“既定法律”。他随后投票推翻该判决，这坐实了人们常从缅因州民主党人那里听到的指控——柯林斯只是表达“关切”，但在关键时刻没有对抗特朗普。

再加上她身上的负担：这个美国最乡村化的州之一创纪录的柴油价格，以及与该州最大国际贸易伙伴加拿大的贸易战。然后，9月22日，调查新闻机构ProPublica在缅因州占据了头条，详细报道了几年前一家国防承包商利用竞选捐款换取联邦资金的阴谋。柯林斯的办公室否认了任何不当行为，并表示已退还捐款。“这些问题已于2021年解决，”她的办公室说。该报道强化了她的民主党对手特洛伊·杰克逊的竞选信息。“你不应该能凭钱包买下政府，”他在ProPublica报道出现前一天的斯卡伯勒活动中宣称。

杰克逊正在以全美民主党人本周期所拥抱的民粹主义经济信息进行竞选，谴责被操纵的制度、高物价和埃隆·马斯克。但他不同寻常之处在于拥有该党迫切希望包装的工人阶级资历。他的竞选通讯中，总是把他的全名前加上“第五代伐木工”，就像人们会给人冠以“博士”或“总理”头衔一样。然而，杰克逊也有弱点，包括在竞选演说时倾向于嘟囔和跑题。民主党人因他们之前提名的候选人格雷厄姆·普拉特纳在丑闻中崩溃而泄气，那是一位极具感染力的候选人。“他有天赋，显然会有所作为，”一位民主党人环顾斯卡伯勒活动现场的人群，觉得不尽如人意。“如果是格雷厄姆·普拉特纳，你会挤不进去。”（他要求匿名，因为他认识柯林斯本人。）一些民主党人担心，对于作为该党基本盘的受过大学教育的专业人士来说，杰克逊的“真实性”可能过头了。“人们心里想，‘天哪，第五代？’”一位民主党内部人士说。“难道第四代或第五代就不能离开伐木业吗？”与普拉特纳不同，杰克逊不太像是明确的反建制选择，因为他在州立法机构任职已达20年。

尽管2020年民调落后（正如现在一样），柯林斯仍以超过八个百分点赢得了那场选举，而特朗普以超过九个百分点输掉了缅因州。要终结缅因州的分裂代表团，以及与之相伴的参议院中最后几个温和派共和党影响力之一，需要一股强大的民主党浪潮。另一方面，如此大的浪潮也可能在俄亥俄、爱荷华、堪萨斯、得克萨斯和阿拉斯加等共和党州重新产生分裂代表团，从而在民主党内创造一股新的温和力量——以及随之而来的更多在参议院努力开展两党合作的动力。我们可以期待。■

item.content:encoded:
独裁者的实验室：纳伊布·布克尔大力推行人工智能

美洲 | 萨尔瓦多 2026年9月24日

萨尔瓦多的年轻总统纳伊布·布克尔非常注重形象。他不愿被看作一个平庸的独裁者，因此不仅将自己包装成这个600万人口国家的救世主，还把自己塑造为一个实验室的建造者——这个实验室常常以技术为驱动，可供他人借鉴。距离明年2月的选举还有几个月，但布克尔丝毫不用担心投票结果。自从七年前萨尔瓦多人首次将他推上总统宝座以来，他已经用盟友塞满了宪法法院，废除了总统任期限制，将市镇数量从262个减至44个，将立法机构席位从84个缩减至60个，并重新划分了选区——这一切都对他有利。此外，他确实仍然广受欢迎。但他更希望在取得新的成功之后面对选民。萨尔瓦多一位不愿透露姓名的分析人士说，总统希望被视为“社会变革的导师”。这一变革的目标是教育和医疗。人工智能的部署是关键。

去年，布克尔在171所学校启动了一个试点项目，使用埃隆·马斯克的xAI公司开发的聊天机器人Grok来辅助教学。Grok充当数学、科学和阅读方面的辅导老师，按照学生自己的节奏进行教学，并由教师监督。其他地方也在进行类似的实验——哥伦比亚在农村地区试点了Meta的聊天机器人——但官员们表示，萨尔瓦多是首个尝试全国全面推广的国家。布克尔正在扩大这一计划。

医疗领域也在进行类似的改造。去年11月，布克尔与谷歌合作推出了DoctorSV应用程序，只需按一下按钮就能联系医生。在人工智能作为第一道筛选的辅助下，这些医生可以诊断疾病、开具处方、安排并分析检查，而且全部免费。政府表示，已有150万萨尔瓦多人注册，并开出了200万张电子处方。布克尔夸口说，这将成为“世界上最好的医疗系统”。

布克尔需要另一个成功故事。他在让国家变得更安全方面不折不扣地兑现了承诺——尽管以民主为代价。他暂停了人权保障，监禁了近2%的人口，往往仅凭涉嫌与帮派有牵连就定罪。2019年他上台时，凶杀案已经在下降，但谋杀率从当年的每10万人38起降至2025年的1.3起。这为他带来了90%左右的支持率——以及国际赞誉。没有人能否认这改变了人们的生活。38岁的母亲约翰娜·菲格罗亚说，我们的孩子们“很幸运”，不必经历那种上车或下车都要提心吊胆的日子。

其他政策则表现不佳。他上一个重大科技赌注——2021年让萨尔瓦多成为第一个将比特币作为法定货币的国家——最终不了了之。普通人发现它没什么用。布克尔将其视为个人项目，还说过一句名言：他在浴室里买比特币。没有人知道，如果有一天他下台，这个国家的比特币储备会变成什么样。与此同时，经济在纸面上看起来比街头感受到的要好。大多数分析师预测今年GDP增长在5%左右，但收益并不均衡。对获得政府合同的人来说是好事，对普通萨尔瓦多人来说则不那么乐观。外国直接投资并未起飞。

萨尔瓦多人注意到了这一点。在5月份圣萨尔瓦多中美洲大学（UCA）进行的一项民意调查中，超过70%的人将经济问题列为主要关切（仅有2%提到犯罪）。布克尔抬高了自己的标杆。这位分析人士说：“他在安全问题上的信誉太高，以至于人们认为他能解决任何其他问题。”

现在评判这些新计划还为时过早。教育实验已获得初步好评。根据该项目资助方之一世界银行的数据，在针对15岁学生的全球阅读、数学和科学能力测试PISA中，试点学校的志愿者学生在2022年的表现与德国和瑞典的平均学生大致相当。但没有证据表明这一成绩水平归功于人工智能的使用——何况被选中的学校里的志愿者学生本来就更有可能是高表现者。世界银行称这些结果“令人惊讶且非常鼓舞人心”。

在首都圣萨尔瓦多的梅赛德斯·金特罗学校门口接孩子的家长们赞不绝口。菲格罗亚女士说，她9岁的女儿取得了“显著”进步。“以前是书本、书本、书本。现在她更有热情了。”

DoctorSV尚未经过独立评估，但得到了拉丁美洲和加勒比开发银行的大力支持，该银行正在为其提供资金。该银行声称，萨尔瓦多已经建立了一个“基于尖端技术的普惠、可持续的医疗系统”。用户也印象深刻。24岁的安德烈亚·巴尔加斯说：“它更快。有一天我感觉非常不舒服，它让我去做了检查并拿到了药——全都免费。”

布克尔在总统府直接运作这两个项目。教育部一名官员描述了官僚被边缘化、几乎无法接触试点学校的情况。许多教师已被解雇。萨尔瓦多教育专家奥斯卡·皮卡多说，改善学校的行之有效的方法是培训教师，而不是发放电子设备。他援引瑞典作为警示案例，该国已开始将屏幕从课堂中撤下，重新回归书本。

医疗工会称这款应用是“创可贴”，无法解决药品和专科医生短缺的问题。数千名公共卫生工作者已被解雇，部分原因是为了缩减政府工资支出并满足IMF贷款的条件。成本也不清楚。xAI没有披露其与政府协议的金额。萨尔瓦多国民议会批准了总额5.76亿美元的贷款，用于教育项目和DoctorSV第二阶段，整个过程没有真正的辩论。

最大的担忧是，布克尔有利用政策积累权力的前科。一些人担心，这项实验实际上是把儿童和病人的个人数据交给他自己和科技公司。国内外很多人都希望这些政策能真正成功。但如果布克尔抱怨自己得不到信任，那也是事出有因。■

item.content:encoded:
唐纳德·特朗普与德尔西·罗德里格斯之间的亲密关系

美洲 | 委内瑞拉 2026年9月24日

唐纳德·特朗普咧嘴笑着，竖起大拇指，与德尔西·罗德里格斯合影留念。罗德里格斯是那个几乎摧毁了委内瑞拉的酷刑、窃取选举的政权的重要成员。特朗普于9月22日在联合国大会上会见了委内瑞拉未经选举产生的临时总统罗德里格斯女士。对特朗普来说，这次纽约会面是一个展示外交政策成功的机会。对罗德里格斯女士而言，这是一个迷住特朗普的黄金机会，希望他能无视反对派对选举的要求，继续青睐她那个听话的威权体制。她的策略显然正在奏效。

今年1月，美国特种部队将前独裁者尼古拉斯·马杜罗从他加拉加斯的住所中拖出，并把他关进了纽约的一座监狱。次日，特朗普威胁当时还是马杜罗副总统的罗德里格斯女士，称如果她不配合，她的下场将“比马杜罗更惨”。如今，她却在距离马杜罗被关押处七英里外与特朗普亲热握手，这凸显了她的生存本能、意识形态的灵活性，以及她几乎做了特朗普想要的一切这一事实。她如此顺从，部分原因是特朗普政府控制着委内瑞拉的全部石油收入。最重要的是，她帮助美国攫取了这些石油。她的政府迅速修改了委内瑞拉的碳氢化合物法律，以欢迎更多美国投资。随后，上月她做了一笔庞大而可疑的交易，通过一家私营公司授予美国政府开发17个油田的权利，并以低廉价格获得这些油田可能产出的大部分石油。鉴于特朗普对石油和谄媚服从的偏爱，这对那些支持选举的人来说是个坏消息。

特朗普与罗德里格斯女士之间的关系是影响委内瑞拉民主未来的关键因素，但并非唯一重要的因素。委内瑞拉部分反对派与该政权之间在加拉加斯的第二轮谈判预计将于本周结束。这些谈判由美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥监督，他似乎比特朗普更热衷于举行选举。第一轮谈判以承诺更换整个最高法院而结束，这对监督公正投票至关重要。第二轮谈判开始时，政权开放了对一些独立媒体网站的访问。预计还将就废除用于打压反对派政治人物的压制性法律进行更多讨论。

此事在美国也有影响。共和党参议员伯尼·莫雷诺呼吁明年7月举行委内瑞拉选举。在居住着许多委内瑞拉人的佛罗里达州，特朗普拥抱一位遭人痛恨的独裁者副手，可能会在中期选举中伤害一些共和党候选人。民主党人要求举行选举，并承诺如果赢得众议院，将调查委内瑞拉政策。这些政界人士仍对流亡的反对派领袖玛丽亚·科里纳·马查多抱有信念。据报道，就在特朗普与德尔西会面之前，她曾三次试图返回委内瑞拉，但均告失败。她在委内瑞拉的出现将加大对选举的压力。特朗普政府至少两次阻止了她真正回国，她目前仍留在巴拿马。在这一局面改变之前，取悦特朗普的罗德里格斯女士似乎坐稳了权力之位。■

item.content:encoded:
美国正在退出一个它从未能重塑的地区

中東與非洲 | 美國的三十五年戰爭 2026年9月24日

當世界領導人於1991年9月齊聚聯合國大會時，美國在中東不受挑戰的霸權時代似乎就在眼前。五角大廈剛剛與眾多盟友打了一場速戰速決的戰爭，將佔領科威特的伊拉克軍隊驅逐出境。美國外交官正準備主持馬德里會議，這是以色列與其若干阿拉伯鄰國之間的首次直接會談。隨著蘇聯奄奄一息，美國看起來準備好在這個動盪地區塑造新的秩序。

然而，隨之而來的卻是35年的混亂，美國從一個軍事蠢行搖擺到另一個軍事蠢行。最近的一次，即唐納德·特朗普與伊朗的衝突，原本打算在幾天內結束，但現在已進入第八個月。它給特朗普最親密的阿拉伯盟友以及世界其他地區帶來了巨大代價。對於本週齊聚紐約聯合國的大人物們來說，美國看起來不像中東困境的解決方案：它就是困境的根源之一。這將是這場戰爭的持久後果之一，無論它何時或如何結束。

儘管美國不會離開中東，但它將不得不從其作為首要強國的角色中退後一步。其盟友已失去信心，其選民已精疲力竭，其戰略家將需要應對其他地方日益嚴重的危機。沒有誰準備好填補這一角色，阿拉伯國家尤其不可能。這將帶來混亂的時代——但從長遠來看，美國時代的終結未必是壞事。

不過，就目前而言，目標只是結束戰爭。美國和伊朗於9月22日在聯合國進行了三個小時的間接會談，卡塔爾特使在兩者之間傳遞信息。這是他們自6月以來的首次此類會談。特朗普先生稱其“非常富有成效”。但他也在大會演講中重申了“消滅”伊朗的威脅。私下裡，外交官對會談不那麼熱情。會談讓雙方有機會重申各自立場，但這種形式很難促成突破——而且雙方立場相距甚遠。伊朗希望美國回到6月簽署的短命協議《諒解備忘錄》（MOU）。特朗普先生則傾向於廢除MOU——它原本只是60天的臨時協議——並談判新的東西。

美國總統還會見了海灣國家以及土耳其和其他四個阿拉伯國家的官員。信息同樣混合：他引用“大量動能”朝向達成協議，同時也警告可能轟炸伊朗的核設施。與此同時，雙方繼續經濟戰。伊朗在過去一週內襲擊了霍爾木茲海峽至少五艘油輪。9月23日，美國對為伊朗飛機加油或提供服務的外國公司實施制裁，這實際上將禁止伊朗航空公司飛往大多數海外目的地。

伊朗戰爭拖延之際，也門戰爭升級。本月，伊朗支持的叛軍組織胡塞武裝放棄了2022年與沙特支持的對手之間的停火協議。他們奪取了也門西南海岸的一大塊地區。這使他們更牢牢控制著連接紅海與亞丁灣的曼德海峽，他們已在該水域試圖對沙特船隻實施封鎖。胡塞武裝還恢復了對沙特阿拉伯本身的襲擊。9月15日，沙特王國稱在伊斯蘭聖城麥加附近攔截了一架無人機。四天後，一枚胡塞導彈擊中了利雅得機場的一個燃料箱，這是多年來他們對沙特首都的首次襲擊。另外，伊拉克民兵襲擊了該王國最重要的石油管道，使其停止服務超過一週（於9月22日恢復運營）。

然而，這些都沒有使油價升至災難性水平——這是伊朗希望用來向特朗普施壓以達成協議的主要槓桿。布倫特原油價格在胡塞攻勢和管道襲擊後攀升至每桶109美元，隨後回落。本刊付印時約為102美元。當然，這個數字並不能說明全部情況：更廣泛的能源市場狀況不佳。幾個月內交貨的“即期”布倫特原油價格本月突破了每桶130美元。成品油稀缺，美國柴油均價現已達到每加侖6.52美元的歷史高位。但特朗普先生立場堅定，即使燃料價格可能使他的共和黨在11月中期選舉中遭受重創。

美國方面仍希望經濟壓力能迫使伊朗屈服。其對伊朗航運的兩個月封鎖正在造成混亂。伊朗港口停擺，正努力通過陸路路線轉移貿易：數百輛卡車在邊境排隊數日。里亞爾接連創下新低。通貨膨脹接近三位數。禁飛伊朗航空公司將擾亂該國的藥品供應鏈。伊朗總統馬蘇德·佩澤什基安承認了危機的嚴重性。議會議長穆罕默德·巴格爾·卡利巴夫抱怨拒絕外交的強硬派。但與特朗普先生一樣，該政權願意承受更多痛苦。

雙方都無法將戰爭決定性地扭轉為對自己有利。華盛頓、德黑蘭和海灣地區的觀點是，戰爭將拖到年底。沙特王儲穆罕默德·本·薩勒曼告訴美國人不要急於回到MOU。他更希望他們維持封鎖並尋求新協議。大多數海灣國家持相同看法（卡塔爾和阿曼是例外）。伊朗不急於達成可能降低油價並在中期選舉前給特朗普提振的協議。摩根大通銀行的分析師已放棄預測接下來會發生什麼。“我們根本不知道如何為終局建模，”他們在9月17日寫道。

這不是美國第一次笨拙地陷入中東泥潭。過去幾十年裡，它幾乎嘗試了該地區每一種軍事干預方式。它派出龐大地面部隊推翻伊拉克的獨裁者，利用空中力量推翻利比亞的獨裁者，武裝敘利亞叛軍，並支持2015年對也門開戰的沙特領導的聯盟。其中一些成功實現了政權更迭，但留下了混亂。另一些則徹底失敗。沒有一個產生有利於美國利益的結果。儘管如此，後果還是有限的。推翻薩達姆·侯賽因對伊拉克人來說是一場災難，他們陷入了多年的宗派流血衝突。通過消除伊朗的主要地區敵人，它使伊斯蘭共和國得以在敘利亞和黎巴嫩建立影響力。但它對美國在該地區最親密盟友的即時影響很小。

這次戰爭不同。在伊朗之外，最嚴重的後果落在了美國的海灣盟友身上。大多數國家的經濟將在2026年萎縮。它們因石油和天然氣銷售損失、旅遊收入消失和基礎設施受損而損失了數千億美元。它們曾希望MOU能讓它們在第四季度恢復正常業務。相反，它們正在私下辯論是否再次推遲大型活動，從科技會議到一級方程式賽車。在海灣之外，戰爭還引發了全球感受到的能源衝擊。而且它在美國人中格外不受歡迎。60%的美國人花了四年時間才將入侵伊拉克視為錯誤。特朗普的伊朗戰爭在不到兩個月內就達到了這一比例。

所有這些因素都將限制美國未來在該地區的角色。首先是其盟友。它們之前有過尖銳分歧：沙特人曾敦促喬治·W·布什在2003年不要入侵伊拉克，巴拉克·奧巴馬在2011年敦促長期埃及獨裁者胡斯尼·穆巴拉克下台時海灣國家感到不安（穆巴拉克大概也是如此）。這些爭端或許使它們質疑美國的判斷，但其承諾和能力從未被懷疑。然後是敘利亞。當奧巴馬先生2013年未能執行針對巴沙爾·阿薩德使用化學武器的“紅線”時，美國看起來優柔寡斷；當它最終未能推翻敘利亞獨裁者時，它看起來很虛弱。在伊朗支持的針對海灣國家的一系列襲擊之後——2019年對沙特油田的打擊，2022年在阿布扎比的致命無人機襲擊——幾乎沒有引起回應，疑慮進一步增加。特朗普先生發動了美國長期試圖遏止的海灣戰爭，摧毀了剩餘的任何信任。

海灣地區沒有人準備好公開討論美國在該地區基地的未來（見地圖）。“現在絕對不是進行此類對話的時候，”一位外交官說。談論關閉一些基地（其中許多在戰爭中被伊朗打擊）甚至縮減它們，會讓美國看起來像是在盟友危難之時拋棄他們。但戰爭可能促使美國遠離維持大型永久性設施。例如，其巴林海軍基地是中东罕见的一個“隨軍家屬”崗位，軍人可攜帶家屬。它不太可能恢復到以前容納近萬人的規模。戰前，卡塔爾準備花費100億美元升級烏代德空軍基地——多哈城外作為美國中央司令部地區總部的基地。它仍願意投入這筆資金；美國是否想要則不清楚。幾個國家的官員表示，他們希望就這些基地可能的使用方式談判新規則。他們已經開始施加臨時限制：沙特阿拉伯在5月阻止了重新開放霍爾木茲海峽的努力，因為它禁止美國戰機進入其領空。

在該地區其他地方，美國已經在退出。它今年春天完成了從敘利亞基地的撤離，伊拉克基地計劃在9月底前清空（這兩個計劃都早於戰爭）。其敵人也有發言權。想像一個最壞情況：特朗普與伊朗的戰爭導致一個核武裝政權能夠對霍爾木茲交通行使否決權。在這種情況下，美國將難以維持在濱海海灣國家的基地。在另一個極端，如果該政權垮台，對這些基地的需求就會減少：一個沒有伊斯蘭共和國的中東將對美國利益遠不那麼敵對。

無論戰爭如何結束，伊朗都不會是美國唯一的威脅。美國在中東的干預主義高峰時期恰逢其他地方相對平靜的一段時期。歐洲大體和平；中國是崛起中的大國，但還不足以在太平洋挑戰美國。首次由奧巴馬先生提出的“重返亞洲”在華盛頓成為一個反覆出現的笑話：每次轉向都是360度轉彎。然而，今天的世界看起來危險得多。五角大廈難以承受將五分之一的航母綁在海灣或耗盡數百枚稀缺的攔截器和導彈來對抗伊朗。

國內政治將提供進一步制約。自林登·約翰遜升級美國在越南的角色以來，還沒有一位總統如此徹底地用一場對外戰爭毀掉自己的任期。特朗普先生的潛在繼任者會注意到這點。共和黨提名的可能領跑者J.D.萬斯是中东戰爭的直言不諱的懷疑者。他幾位可能的民主黨對手也是如此。再加上對以色列日益惡化的看法：皮尤5月民調發現，62%的美國人對以色列政府持負面看法，比2022年上升19個百分點。曾幫助塑造美國中東政策的親以色列共識正在消退。

收縮不是撤退。美國將在中東保留利益。反恐是一個罕見的各方都能同意的話題：當伊斯蘭國威脅黎凡特時，甚至美國和伊朗也發現自己站在同一邊作戰。一個參與度降低的美國仍可能對基地組織和其他團體發動打擊。它將繼續向盟友出售武器、談判貿易協議和主持和平談判。對以色列的軍事援助可能持續多年，儘管一些民調顯示多數美國人反對。

將改變的是美國作為該地區安全保障者和問題解決者的觀念——正如一位海灣官員所說，“我們有任何問題隨時打電話給華盛頓”。也門最近的事件讓我們得以一窺這意味著什麼。特朗普先生不僅多次拒絕穆罕默德王子對也門發動空襲的請求。他的代表還在阿曼與胡塞特使交談，後者承諾遵守2025年停火協議並避免襲擊紅海中的美國船隻。後者可能是獨特的特朗普式操作：很難想像其他總統會與被指定的恐怖分子達成私下協議。但這種不願介入的態度會比他更長久。

地區之外沒有人能填補這一真空。歐洲太弱。應沙特阿拉伯的請求，英國只提供了一架空中加油機。俄羅斯既沒有手段（它深陷烏克蘭），也沒有意願（它向胡塞提供了幫助，主要是為了刁難美國）。它將自己視為地區動盪的受益者，而不是終結者。中國近年來沒有在邊界以外進行嚴重軍事行動的經驗。

剩下的就是地區國家，其中最強大的是三個非阿拉伯國家。伊朗有導彈和代理人，而以色列擁有中東最強大的軍隊。在某種意義上，它們是镜像：強大到足以破壞地區秩序，但不足以建立一個秩序。第三個是土耳其，一個軍事和外交大國，也是一個日益增長的武器出口國。它此前曾果斷干預衝突。最終推翻阿薩德先生的叛軍在土耳其保護下多年；2019年土耳其軍隊擊退了試圖奪取利比亞首都的軍閥。但土耳其人受到伊朗、以色列和許多阿拉伯國家的猜疑。

短期內，該地區可能會分裂為幾個集團，因為阿拉伯國家與非阿拉伯大國結盟。長期穩定將要求它們發揮更大作用。要做到這一點，它們需要更好的軍隊、更強大的聯盟，以及最難以捉摸的東西：合作。有一些早期跡象表明它們認識到變革的必要性——至少是海灣地區穩定而富有的國家。以軍隊為例。海灣國家幾十年來一直在購買昂貴的美國軍事裝備。並非所有裝備對它們最終打的戰爭都有用。隨著購物清單的變化，它們將尋找新供應商。伊朗展示了彈道導彈計劃的價值。沙特不能從美國購買彈道導彈，但它已經從中國獲得了導彈（本月可能已對胡塞使用了）。阿拉伯世界的每個國家都渴望從土耳其這個主要生產國購買無人機。今年早些時候，阿聯酋簽署了一項為期十年的購買烏克蘭無人機的協議。該協議包括共同生產條款：它們將建造新工廠來製造。這符合阿聯酋和其他地方日益增長的在本國生產武器的努力。

它們也在尋找新盟友。自7月以來，沙特宣布與巴基斯坦和土耳其達成共同防禦協議，並與十幾個國家組成確保紅海安全的海上聯盟。就軍事條約而言，這些是模糊而志向遠大的。海上聯盟包括孟加拉國，該國距離5000公里且缺乏實質性的藍水海軍。但它們顯示了方向。還會有更多這類臨時聯盟。有些會短命。另一些可能持久。

最重要的是，阿拉伯國家需要就它們想要什麼樣的地區達成一致。10月7日之前，常聽到海灣官員談論“新中東”——一個更專注於賺錢而非打仗的中東。這是一個美好的想法，但在一個充滿棘手衝突和無能政府的地區卻難以置信。今天，沙特和阿聯酋甚至無法在也門合作，儘管胡塞武裝對兩者都構成危險。阿拉伯聯盟和海灣合作委員會（六個石油君主國的俱樂部）都沒有發展成有用的機構。

這些缺點是美國時代在中東的必然後果。美國及其地區盟友從未共享崇高議程。沒有像二戰後歐洲那樣的自由民主計劃將它們聯繫在一起。美國也沒有促進它在亞洲追求的那種經濟增長。它只想保持石油流通、保護以色列並維持其基地（後來又增加了打擊聖戰分子）。這些目標都不需要阿拉伯國家有能力或繁榮；事實上，有些目標如果它們不繁榮反而更容易實現。這對其盟友來說沒問題，它們大多只關心政權的維持。它在一段時間內實現了所有這些目標。但今天，它的基地受到重創，它的油輪受到攻擊，它最親密的盟友以色列已經打了三年仗。即使特朗普先生沒有魯莽地打破它，美國在過去35年裡建立的東西也根本不持久：該地區太多國家是弱小、分裂或失敗的國家。沒有長期保障者可以依靠，也許它們現在必須自己建立更好的東西。■

item.content:encoded:
How realistic is Africa’s dream of a gas-powered future?

Middle East & Africa | Gambling on gas

Sep 24th 2026

To tell the story of African gas, Alain Ebobissé explains, he carries his “gas map” with him everywhere. The boss of Africa50, an infrastructure investment platform, produces a sheet of paper showing the world laced with pipelines. Africa is almost entirely blank (see map). “Look at that!” Mr Ebobissé exclaims. “We have almost no pipelines, no infrastructure—it’s terrible.” Africa holds 13% of the world’s natural-gas reserves, with deposits in 24 of its 54 countries and more still to be found. Yet it burns less than 5% of the gas used for power worldwide. Its pipeline network is one-tenth as dense as North America’s. “Who is using that gas?” Mr Ebobissé asks. “It’s not us.”

Politicians, business leaders and investors across the continent hope that using more gas will spur industrialisation and growth. “The objective isn’t just to produce more gas: the objective is to make sure that you have more productive economies across Africa,” says Olu Verheijen, the energy adviser to Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu. Volatility in global energy markets because of wars in Ukraine and in the Gulf, combined with a reduced focus on net-zero targets, has renewed interest in gas. But in Africa, it may not live up to the hype.

To its African champions, gas could solve many energy problems. Currently generating 14% of electricity south of the Sahara, the fuel could grow in importance as coal, the largest source at 40%, declines. Cheap solar power may prove a readier source of electricity for the 600m Africans who still do without. But the flexibility of natural gas means it is useful in almost every corner of a modern economy: as a heat source for steel plants and cement factories, and as a feedstock for fertilisers and petrochemicals. Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) can replace dirtier kerosene and charcoal in household stoves. Compressed natural gas (CNG) offers drivers a cheaper, cleaner alternative to petrol and diesel. For big producers such as Nigeria, exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Europe and Asia also bring in scarce hard currency.

Partly because sub-Saharan Africa lacks pipelines, processing plants, storage tanks and the like, the potential of gas remains largely hypothetical. Some 43% of what was produced in 2025 was shipped abroad rather than used at home. Of the natural gas Africa does consume, nearly half is used to generate electricity, a higher share than elsewhere. Just 17% goes to industry, compared with nearly 40% in South America and more than 30% in Asia. Only nine sub-Saharan African cities have piped gas, says Marc Howard of African Energy, a consultancy. New pipelines struggle to attract investment without guaranteed demand from buyers, such as gas-fired power stations, which in turn find it hard to raise capital without a secure supply of gas.

Could the current interest in gas change that? So far the promise is most encouraging upstream, where international energy firms including France’s TotalEnergies and Italy’s ENI are ramping up plans to draw more LNG from the continent. Multiple LNG projects are under way in Mozambique, home to Africa’s third-largest reserves, including one worth $20bn which was stalled for years due to an insurgency in the country’s north. In Nigeria, thanks to home-grown firms like Seplat and Oando, annual gas production could grow to around 11bn cubic feet a day—about 114bn cubic metres (bcm) a year—by 2030, according to Pranav Joshi of Rystad, a consultancy. Africa’s total gas production in 2025 was an estimated 262bcm, up by 2.5% on the previous year.

Growing African demand for gas, particularly where countries are shifting away from dirtier coal, is beginning to spur investment further downstream, too. South Africa is accelerating plans to build gas plants, LNG import terminals and other gas infrastructure that could be worth $9.5bn in total, says Paul Eardley-Taylor of Standard Bank. Nivedh Thaikoottathil, also of Rystad, reckons that sub-Saharan Africa’s total capacity for gas-power generation could reach 52 gigawatts (GW) by 2035, up from 26GW today, if new developments in South Africa and Nigeria, and smaller but strategically important projects in Mozambique, Tanzania and Ivory Coast, come online.

That is more than coal, with an estimated capacity of 35GW in 2035, but dwarfed by solar (140GW). It is also not guaranteed. Cash-strapped African utilities are unreliable customers for relatively expensive power from gas plants. The Natural Resource Governance Institute, a think-tank in New York, found that in Nigeria, now halfway through its “Decade of Gas” initiative, most new production is set to be exported—in part because the country’s failing electricity grid limits what the government can buy from gas-power generators. “The real constraint is on distribution,” admits Ms Verheijen.

Nor are upstream gas firms necessarily willing suppliers. In Tanzania and Senegal, negotiations with international energy firms have been hampered by disagreements over how much gas should be allocated to domestic markets, and on what commercial terms. “Why would they want to invest in a country that says it wants to cap prices, regulate prices, and take them outside the global market?” asks Jan Rosenow of Oxford University.

A few firms have managed to overcome the chicken-and-egg dilemma that bedevils investment in domestic gas infrastructure. Genser Energy, a Ghanaian operator, has laid over 400km of pipeline in Ghana, mostly to supply gas to gold mines. It has since built a natural-gas liquids terminal and gas-conditioning plant, and recently raised half a billion dollars to expand its portfolio of power projects in west Africa.

Gas-powered industrial clusters that are common in north Africa are also beginning to sprout below the Sahara. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial capital, “became an industrial hub because gas pipelines were available”, argues Sumeet Singh of Powergas, which delivers CNG to businesses across the country. Reliable gas supply does indeed help explain why Sacvin, a plastic manufacturer with factories near Lagos, has expanded in recent years, says its managing director, Jogesh Khatwani. Bustling industrial districts on the outskirts of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania’s biggest city, are powered by domestic gas.

In theory, the global gas crunch should multiply such effects by making it easier to raise capital for new African gas projects. The World Bank and other multilateral lenders have relaxed their rules on energy financing, allowing for the funding of gas as well as renewables. Armel Simondin, the boss of Perenco, an Anglo-French energy firm with projects across central Africa, expects this to “unlock projects that were completely blocked at some point”.

But starting many projects at once is itself risky. A future global gas glut could expose higher-cost African producers to losses. Technological advances, such as longer-duration battery storage, could make gas uncompetitive with renewables, leaving some investments stranded. Long-term energy forecasts are unreliable—so a big bet on gas is a high-stakes gamble. ■

item.content:encoded:
一场灾难性的新战争威胁着非洲

中东与非洲 | 重回流血冲突 2026年9月24日 就在几年前，2020年至2022年间，埃塞俄比亚最北部的提格雷地区爆发了一场内战。据估计有数十万人丧生。这场战争使埃塞俄比亚和厄立特里亚的军队与提格雷执政党提格雷人民解放阵线（TPLF）形成对峙。由于“严重的人权侵犯”，美国于2021年对埃塞俄比亚实施武器禁运，并对厄立特里亚军队、高级官员及国有企业实施制裁。幸运的是，这场危机终于结束了——至少美国官员是这么说的。9月18日，美国解除了对埃塞俄比亚的武器禁运，并未延续对厄立特里亚的制裁。美国财政部宣布：“（埃塞俄比亚的）国家紧急状态已经结束。”这一时机颇为蹊跷。9月23日，效忠提格雷人民解放阵线的武装力量夺取了提格雷地区三个机场的控制权，促使埃塞俄比亚联邦政府暂停了前往该地区的航班。TPLF指责埃塞俄比亚军队对提格雷南部发动攻击，并声称其部队已“进入防御性战争”。一名埃塞俄比亚官员则表示，TPLF实际上“对邻近阿姆哈拉和阿法尔地区的军队阵地发动了全面进攻”。截至本文发稿时，这两个地区以及提格雷南部均似乎爆发了激烈战斗。 一年多来，TPLF与埃塞俄比亚总理阿比·艾哈迈德之间的紧张关系不断加剧。TPLF指责阿比先生将提格雷置于惩罚性围困之下，称这是针对其人民的“种族灭绝”运动的一部分。与此同时，阿比先生的政府表示，TPLF是敌对势力的“特洛伊木马”，这些势力一心想要肢解埃塞俄比亚——其中最主要的就是厄立特里亚，阿比先生与厄立特里亚也剑拔弩张。近几周，埃塞俄比亚军队对TPLF发动了一场未宣战的无人机战争。而近几天，这似乎已升级为近乎第二次内战的状态。如果战斗持续下去，最新一轮冲突将与上一轮截然不同。当时，厄立特里亚军队与埃塞俄比亚军队并肩作战，共同对抗TPLF。来自提格雷以南阿姆哈拉地区的多支民兵武装——即所谓的“法诺”——也加入了战斗。法诺和厄立特里亚80岁的独裁者伊萨亚斯·阿费沃尔基都感到被阿比先生2022年与TPLF讲和的决定所背叛。法诺于次年对联邦政府发动了叛乱。就伊萨亚斯先生而言，他似乎越来越担心阿比先生反复威胁要吞并厄立特里亚部分海岸线。9月20日，TPLF、法诺与其他五个埃塞俄比亚反政府组织发表联合声明，宣布结成联盟，旨在推翻阿比先生的政权。厄立特里亚官员否认参与该联盟。但伊萨亚斯先生与法诺有长期联系，据称他向TPLF及其他组织提供了武器和后勤支持。局势降级的前景十分渺茫。“战争已经开始了，”一位前埃塞俄比亚情报官员认为。TPLF和法诺似乎正试图包围韦尔迪亚——这是阿姆哈拉北部的一座城镇，位于连接提格雷与亚的斯亚贝巴的主要公路沿线。如果韦尔迪亚失守，可能是叛军向埃塞俄比亚首都发起攻势的前奏。叛军还侵入了阿法尔地区，他们可能试图扰乱甚至阻断通往吉布提港口的公路运输，而这条公路对于埃塞俄比亚几乎所有的国际贸易——包括燃料进口——都至关重要。阿比先生有两个重大优势。第一，各反政府组织单打独斗都相当弱小，整体上又因民族仇恨和历史积怨而四分五裂。这可能妨碍它们的协调能力。阿比先生的另一个优势是空中力量。上一次TPLF抢先逼近亚的斯亚贝巴是在2021年，当时埃塞俄比亚军队用无人机将其击退。如今，阿比先生拥有更大规模、更先进的武器库。今年5月，总理的一名顾问呼吁通过定点无人机袭击刺杀TPLF领导人。“TPLF领导层可能撑不过这个星期，”一位人脉广泛的观察人士表示。然而，阿比先生还有其他敌人需要应对。如果埃塞俄比亚的叛军受挫，伊萨亚斯先生可能会担心自己成为下一个目标，从而命令他的军队参战。厄立特里亚也是苏丹武装部队（SAF）的关键盟友——苏丹武装部队是邻国苏丹的国家军队，该国正深陷自身的灾难性内战。而苏丹武装部队又对埃塞俄比亚支持其敌人快速支援部队感到愤怒。这意味着埃塞俄比亚的战争可能升级为区域性的流血冲突。“这场战争不会局限于提格雷，”一名TPLF官员预测，“它将波及厄立特里亚，也将波及苏丹。” ■ 订阅《非洲分析》周刊，让您随时了解这个世界上最年轻、也最不被理解的大陆的最新动态。

item.title: Why so many Nigerian states want their own airline
item.description:
Middle East & Africa

Middle East & Africa | Flying frenzy Sep 24th 2026 If EBONYI, A poor state in south-eastern Nigeria, is known for anything, it is for the paucity of its development efforts, from reducing poverty to improving literacy. That may be because the state government has been pursuing higher ambitio...
item.content:encoded:
Why so many Nigerian states want their own airline

Middle East & Africa | Flying frenzy

Sep 24th 2026

If EBONYI, A poor state in south-eastern Nigeria, is known for anything, it is for the paucity of its development efforts, from reducing poverty to improving literacy. That may be because the state government has been pursuing higher ambitions: it has been trying to build an airport. It says it spent some 50bn naira ($38m) on it between 2020 and 2023 alone, more than half of what it spent on education in the same period. The project has been marred by corruption allegations and vandalism. After a few flights, air traffic stopped because of a defective runway. Undeterred, Ebonyi’s government is mulling the next step: launching its very own airline.

Nigeria’s state-run airlines have a modest record, to say the least. The state carrier, Nigeria Airways, went bust in the early 2000s amid tales of unpaid salaries and rat-infested cabins. Of those run by state governments, three at least still operate (though only one is profitable). Ebonyi’s proposal is a “joke”, says Chris Aligbe, an aviation analyst. Yet state governors present plans to start their own carriers with some regularity. In July the governor of Kano, a northern state, said a local airline would start operating within the year “by the grace of God”.

State governments are not best placed to run airlines, but a logic of sorts exists for their lofty plans. Nigeria is vast and has terrible road and rail networks, plus a big problem with bandits. Being accessible by air could be a boon for isolated states, especially if it makes them more appealing to rich investors and tourists from Abuja, the capital, and Lagos, the commercial centre.

Such hopes needn’t be pie in the sky. Akwa Ibom, a state in the south, launched an airline in 2019. Ibom Air has helped turn the regional airport into an economic hub and claims to have boosted tourism. It now connects to six destinations outside the state, including Accra, the capital of Ghana, and is building a repair and maintenance facility for west Africa. The aim is to offer the sort of specialised repairs for which African airlines currently have to fly overseas. It is also profitable, bringing in 7bn naira ($5.3m) in profits in 2025. Officials in neighbouring Cross River state hope that their local carrier will tempt tourists to try the state’s seafood and attend its annual carnival.

Yet the economic case for a local airline run by the state government is, in general, hard to fathom. Ebonyi’s struggling airport is an hour’s drive from the terminal in neighbouring Enugu state, which has ample capacity (and its own fledgling airline). Bayelsa, another state in the south, also wants to launch an airline, even though flights from Port Harcourt, 45 minutes across the border in Rivers state, serve it well enough (see map). Though airline capacity is rising, domestic air travel grew by a modest 4% last year. The market remains small, as few Nigerians can afford to fly.

Yet officials have reasons for their obsession with air travel. One is politics. Ebonyi’s airport may be unusable, but the governor who had it built apparently impressed the president enough to be appointed infrastructure minister. Another is money. The federal government sometimes takes over failing regional airports and pays states generous compensation. Spending on airports and airlines is little scrutinised. Ebonyi’s government says it has paid 50bn naira for three planes for its proposed airline. So far, there is no sign of any of them being delivered. ■

item.title: What a beer with no label says about a small African country
item.description:
Middle East & Africa

Middle East & Africa | Pint-sized problems Sep 24th 2026 For centuries São Tomé and Príncipe were known for chattel and chocolate. After the Portuguese landed on the islands in 1470 they brought enslaved Africans to toil on sugar roças (plantations). Portugal ostensibly ended slavery in the ...
item.content:encoded:
What a beer with no label says about a small African country

Middle East & Africa | Pint-sized problems

Sep 24th 2026

For centuries São Tomé and Príncipe were known for chattel and chocolate. After the Portuguese landed on the islands in 1470 they brought enslaved Africans to toil on sugar roças (plantations). Portugal ostensibly ended slavery in the 1870s. But indentured labour on São Tomé and Príncipe continued, making it the world’s largest cacao producer for a time.

These days, to understand Africa’s least populous country after the Seychelles—and one that holds a general election on September 27th—grab a beer. Specifically, an unlabelled brown bottle made by Rosema, the archipelago’s sole brewer. After independence from Portugal in 1975 the country became a Soviet satellite. East Germans helped set up the pilsner-making state entity. Rosema is known as cerveja nacional, a fitting name for a beer that quenches a thirst for post-colonial patriotism—and offers a window into the political economy.

There are few big firms in São Tomé and Príncipe. Dreams of an oil industry and a deep-water port are unfulfilled. But Rosema is always on tap. Since privatisation in 1995, ownership has rocked back and forth like a drunk, between an Angolan businessman and two influential local brothers. Much like a Congolese mine or a Nigerian oil firm, control can oscillate depending on who is in power. In the latest twist, in May the Constitutional Court returned the brewer to the Angolan, Mello Xavier, the fifth shift since 2018. It was seen as proof that Carlos Vila Nova, the president, is consolidating power after dismissing his rival in a palace coup in 2025.

The chicanery in the pint-sized country reflects its weak rule of law, shallow economy and patronage politics. “Beer is part of the lubrication of elections,” says Alex Vines of the European Council on Foreign Relations, a think-tank. As polls loom, candidates are handing out gifts, including beer. Locals call it tomando banho, “taking a shower” (a sticky one).

At Cantinho da tia Cheila, a dusty-pink kiosk-cum-bar on the smaller island of Príncipe, Cheila, the eponymous owner, tips some beer on the floor before pouring one into a glass, a common ritual across Africa and in hip-hop videos from the 1990s. She says Rosema occasionally puts labels on the bottles but they slide off in the humidity. Still, it is cheaper than Portuguese imports and “it gives us pride in our land.”

Her patrons agree. But like many barstool philosophers they dismiss politicians’ promises, shaking their heads as noisy campaign vehicles pass by on the street. They know from experience: it is the hops that kill you.■

item.content:encoded:
俄罗斯对欧洲的灰色地带攻击日益大胆

欧洲 | 提升混合战赌注 2026年9月24日 俄罗斯对欧洲的破坏行动已升级到如此程度，以至于9月18日法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙召集法国政党领袖和总统候选人，就平民伤亡威胁进行通报。据《世界报》报道，马克龙对他们说：“没有人是安全的。”他说，俄罗斯人的目标是“打破我们对乌克兰人的支持”。前一天，波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克援引情报称，俄罗斯打算用无人机或导弹打击支持乌克兰的国家，然后声称这些袭击是意外。他说，俄罗斯想通过测试北约条约第5条来“瘫痪”北约——该条款承诺对一国的攻击将被视为对所有国家的攻击。如果回应软弱，就会让人对这一承诺产生怀疑。

多年来，俄罗斯一直在对欧洲国家进行可否认的挑衅。自2022年全面入侵乌克兰以来，这些挑衅有所增加。其中包括侦察无人机入侵、黑客攻击、纵火、针对货运航班的包裹炸弹，以及暗杀欧洲军火公司高管的阴谋。最近几个月，节奏似乎再次加快。据安全官员称，俄罗斯的行动有三个主要目标：试图胁迫欧洲国家停止对乌克兰的支持；提高提供这种支持的代价；以及试图让北约看起来无能为力。

“感觉我们正在从一系列灰色地带事件转向一场持续性的行动，”英国前外交官安德鲁·汤姆森说，他现在任职于德国安全公司Monarch。就在图斯克和马克龙公开发声前的一周内，意大利战机在执行北约任务时击落了一架从白俄罗斯进入立陶宛的携带爆炸物的无人机，还有其他战机拦截了两架侵犯北约领空的俄罗斯战斗机。同一周，俄罗斯无人机袭击了乌克兰境内距离波兰边境口岸仅2公里的一列火车，而就在不久前，英国前首相鲍里斯·约翰逊刚刚经过那里。在荷兰，铁路网络最近因有人在铁轨上协同放置管道而遭到破坏。更重要的是，8月份，一架携带爆炸物的无人机飞入德国莱比锡-哈勒机场一架用于为乌克兰运输武器的货机，但未能引爆。德国指责俄罗斯发动了这次袭击，并关闭了一个俄罗斯文化中心作为报复。

并非所有此类事件都容易归因。许多行动都设计成可否认的，因此被称为“混合战”或“灰色地带战争”。汤姆森说，实际发生的远比官方报道的多。它们通常针对关键基础设施或国防公司，包括损坏设备的“意外事故”、闯入敏感地点以及招募特工的行为。单个事件可能看起来是随机的，但整体来看，它们显示出一种破坏和情报收集的模式。在许多情况下，破坏活动由当地代理人或犯罪团伙实施。许多人可能不知道他们的雇主是俄罗斯。使用自由职业破坏者的优势在于更难指认俄罗斯的情报机构。劣势在于，由于他们没有受过训练，更有可能搞砸任务。

“模糊性本身就是武器的一部分，”戴维·卡特勒说，他曾任北约情报官员，现在华盛顿智库欧洲政策分析中心任职。对发生了什么的不确定性使各国更难就回应达成一致。这些事件的强度经过精心校准，足以产生影响，但低于会促使北约采取军事行动的门槛。荷兰铁路的混乱就是一个很好的例证。荷兰当局尚未说明这起破坏是否与俄罗斯有关，还是由愤怒的农民所为——他们在同一天的抗议活动中封锁了道路。然而，由于俄罗斯与其他灰色地带事件有关联，即使没有被明确指责，它也能从恐惧和怀疑中获益。

欧洲面临的关键挑战是如何回应。许多国家正在采取防御措施，例如在机场和其他关键基础设施周围安装反无人机防护。一些人认为，欧洲还需要更强有力的措施来提高俄罗斯发动混合攻击的代价。它可以通过进一步限制向俄罗斯人发放签证数量、驱逐外交官、关闭领事馆、实施更严厉的制裁或扣押更多俄罗斯影子舰队油轮来进行报复。波罗的海国家正在推动欧洲没收被冻结的俄罗斯资产以资助乌克兰。其他人建议欧洲应该以牙还牙。德国对外情报机构负责人马丁·耶格在2月份表示，西方需要“更经常地证明我们也能做非常类似的事情，让对方也感受到痛苦”。

诸如网络攻击之类的行动可能已经在进行中。有人推测，法国可能正在做与乌克兰类似的事情——乌克兰正在马里对俄罗斯雇佣军非洲军团进行无人机打击。“莫斯科最尊重的是实力，”卡特勒说。除非欧洲表现出足够的强硬来威慑挑衅，否则俄罗斯将继续升级。到目前为止，它的挑衅还没有造成灾难性后果——但本可能造成。轨道上的障碍物可能导致火车脱轨。机场的无人机袭击可能击落客机。最危险的做法是让俄罗斯不断推进，直到某个地方破裂。■

item.content:encoded:
弗里德里希·默茨，僵尸总理

欧洲 | 默茨黄昏 2026年9月24日 弗里德里希·默茨正在打破一连串不幸的纪录。他是民调历史上最不受欢迎的德国总理。他的基民盟及其巴伐利亚姊妹党（基民盟/基社盟）也正徘徊在历史最低支持率附近。9月20日，在梅克伦堡-前波莫恩州的一场选举中，基民盟首次被逐出州议会，得票率跌破5%。对于总理党内的许多人来说，继本月早些时候基民盟在东部萨克森-安哈尔特州被民粹主义右翼的德国选择党（AfD）彻底击败之后，这最后一场惨败标志着事态已无法挽回。同样在9月20日投票的柏林，基民盟的竞选工作人员报告说，当地民众只愿意谈论他们对默茨先生的厌恶——而默茨甚至不在选票上。死亡的气息笼罩着他的总理任期。然而，尽管所有人都能看到默茨先生脚下的活板门，却没有人准备按下机关。 部分原因是，如果他下台，情况只会更糟。执政各党不想触发可能由德国选择党获胜的提前选举。基民盟/基社盟若将初级联盟伙伴社民党（SPD）踢出政府，组建少数派政府——据报道这是默茨办公室曾考虑过的方案——将在议会中沦为德国选择党的人质。而如果最有可能的替代人选——德国最大州北莱茵-威斯特法伦州的基民盟州长亨德里克·维斯特——不是要在明年4月面临连任竞选的话，更换最高领导人的想法或许会更有吸引力。无论如何，此类总理更迭的制度障碍使其风险重重。“在这个阶段你要是敢露头，就会有人把你的头砍下来，”基民盟成员、政治咨询公司msl负责人维甘·萨拉萨尔表示。这使得默茨先生奇异地获得了自由，得以推进已成为其总理任期标志性议题的工作：完成其政府7月达成的一揽子经济及其他改革。在9月20日投票结束后出人意料的一次讲话中，他誓言要以“骨气、坚定和耐心”推进这些改革。他补充说，这些改革可以成为他所说的渗入德国政治的“威权毒药”的解药（德国选择党在梅克伦堡-前波莫恩州排名第一，极左翼的左党在柏林获胜）。尽管总理倾向于夸大规模并不大的提议，但他日渐减少的支持者群体欣赏他对这些提议的投入。然而，要让这些改革在联邦议院获得通过，需要一种迄今为止总理一直未能展现的圆熟手腕。执政联盟仅享有12席的多数优势，而围绕养老金改革——这一揽子方案中最雄心勃勃的部分——已经出现了零星交火。7月，政府同意废除2014年引入的一项受欢迎因此代价高昂的规定，该规定允许一些工人提前退休并领取全额养老金。劳工部长兼社民党共同领导人贝尔贝尔·巴斯将养老金方案称为“整体艺术作品”（Gesamtkunstwerk），暗示支持其中每一项内容。但梅克伦堡-前波莫恩州的社民党州长马努埃拉·施韦西希将反对该提案作为其竞选的核心议题，她在竞选中与德国选择党几乎打成平手，仅以微弱劣势位居第二。施韦西希女士如今已成为党内一股不可小觑的力量，而本周社民党议员通过的一份文件将选举称为“公平塑造改革的授权”。基民盟议员嗅到危险，誓言保护这一协议。两个党的领导层都未能牢牢掌控其议会党团。确保养老金规定按承诺被废除将是一项重大挑战。养老护理改革和2027年预算的表决也将如此。每一项都为不安分的议员提供了制造麻烦的机会。在基民盟内部打听一番，你会发现一种比默茨先生的困境更深的焦虑。随着民粹主义者在左翼，尤其是右翼的壮大，这个长期以来既视自己为统一力量又视自己为执政力量的政党，对德国政治的碎裂化是否有任何应对之策？“我们需要一些为之奋斗的东西，而不是仅仅反对一切，”一位焦虑的党内人物表示。所有人都同意不可能回到一切照旧的状态。然而，除了寄望于时间流逝带来救赎之外，似乎没有任何替代方案。在4月之前不会再有任何选举。与此同时，经济显示出复苏迹象，默茨先生将有很多机会在国际舞台上大显身手。这些可能会为他赢得几次缓刑。然后呢？■
